sentences.text: NOTE 02. 06.04.2026 BVLNC,J  I.A.No.01 of 2026  Heard Sri C.Prakash Reddy, learned  counsel for the petitioner/appellant/convict  and Sri C.Panini Somayaji, learned Additional  Public Prosecutor representing the State.

Petitioner is the sole accused in  POCSO Sessions Case No.290 of 2022 on  the file of the learned Special Court for  Speedy Trial of Offences under the Protection  of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012,
 Bhimavaram.

entities.text: Protection  of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the  petitioner/appellant/convict would submit that  petitioner/convict was found guilty for the  offence under Section 376 IPC, Section 3 r/w  4 of POCSO Act, 2012, Section 363 and 420  IPC.

Accordingly, he was convicted  U/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentenced to  undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of  ten (10) years and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/-
 (Rupees Ten Thousand only) in default, shall  undergo simple imprisonment for a period of  three (03) months for the offence under (Contd.)
Section 376 IPC and Section3 r/w 4 of  2 POCSO Act, 2012.

He further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven (7) years and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/-
(Rupees Ten Thousand only) in default, shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of three (03) months for the offence under Section 363 IPC.

He further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven CRLA/193/2026 on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143201757/
1 (7) years and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/-
(Rupees Ten Thousand only) in default
, shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of three (03) months for the offence under Section 420 IPC.
All the sentences shall run concurrently.
Learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant/convict would further submit that the petitioner/convict paid the fine amount and filed original receipt along with the appeal grounds.
Learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant/convict would submit that the learned trial Court erroneously convicted the petitioner without appreciating the facts in proper perspective.
Hence, the petitioner preferred the appeal, challenging the judgment on various grounds.
He would further submit that the victim and the appellant were in love and that, as per the  3 case of the prosecution, their parents opposed the same.
The sentence of imprisonment imposed by the trail Court is a fixed sentence of ten (10) years, and there is no possibility of hearing the appeal in the near future.
Therefore, the order of sentence of imprisonment imposed by the trial Court may be suspended, pending disposal of the appeal.
Learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed the application.
However, no written objections filed.

He would admit that the age of victim was around 16 years at the time of offence, as per the case of the prosecution,
and that the victim and the accused were in love for some time, however, their parents opposed the same, and as the victim was a minor, case was filed.
 Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and as the sentence imposed by the trial Court is a fixed sentence of ten (10) years and as there is no possibility of hearing the appeal in the near future "the order of sentence of imprisonment alone imposed by the learned Special Court for Speedy Trial of Offences under the Protection of Children CRLA/193/2026 on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143201757/
2 from Sexual Offences Act, 2012,
Bhimavaram vide judgment dated  4 10.03.2026 in POCSO Sessions Case No.290 of 2022 shall be suspended, pending disposal of the appeal.

and the appellant shall be released on bail subject to the following conditions":
i) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall execute a personal bond for Rs.25,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only), with two (02) sureties for a like sum each, to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.
ii) On such release, the petitioner/ appellant/accused shall appear before the learned trial Court, on every fourth Saturday of the month, till disposal of the Appeal.

iii) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall not intimidate, or contact or annoy the victim or her family members in any manner.
iv) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall not leave the country without permission of the Court.
v) If the petitioner/appellant/accused violates any of the above conditions, the prosecution is at liberty to file an application seeking cancellation of the bail.
Accordingly, the application is ordered.
________ BVLNC,J Heard.
Admit.
Registry is directed to prepare paper booklet, as soon as trial Court record is received.
List the matter in the month of June 2026 under the caption "Final Hearing".
BVLNC ,

J NOTE:
Issue C.C. by today B/o.
